_README: Multilingual moderation corpus. Generated by an LLM red-team pass, then curated: terms with a common benign meaning were removed from the blocking tier. Every decision and its reason is in curation_decisions. profanities/evasions MUST be caught by the Tier 2 matcher; negative_controls MUST NOT be blocked by Tier 1.

curation_decisions._comment: Tier 1 curation decisions over the LLM-generated corpus. 'drop_term' = the term has a common benign meaning, so Tier 1 (which blocks on send) must not carry it; Tier 2's LLM judges it in context instead. 'allowlist' = the term stays in the Tier 2 matcher, but a specific benign word that matched it by prefix is exempted there. 'restored_controls' = negative controls that were once retired and are now live again; every one of them must be listed under its language and must not be blocked by Tier 1. There is no bucket for retiring a control, and that is deliberate. 'tier2_known_flags' = the controls the recall-oriented Tier 2 matcher still flags; Tier 2 does not block, so this is a note and not an excuse, and the list is here so that adding one is an edit to this record.

_known_gaps.cs/sk pica: Closed. Tier 1 no longer strips diacritics, so 'pica' and 'píča' are distinct tokens, and bare 'pica' is Tier 2 only because Catalan, Portuguese and Spanish all use it.
_known_gaps.native review: The wordlist and these curation decisions were LLM-generated and curated by a single non-native curator. No native speaker has reviewed any language. The collision gate catches frequency-detectable homographs only; register, regional sense and reclaimed usage are invisible to it.
